liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Stella Blue** (1 review): The seventh take of Stella Blue is highlighted as really great by the listener [15]
- **Wharf Rat** (1 review): Wharf Rat provides a special element to the show, alongside good Supplication and Slipknot [11]

## The recordings

- **gd76-07-12.sbd.aj.7771.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 36 songs; 218 min; rated 3.73/5 by 11 [1]. Said about its sound: Second set is recommended for fans of 1976 performances, though overall quality is not extraordinary; Soundcheck segment featuring Eyes of the World has superior audio compared to the main show [9][10]
- **gd1976-07-12.sbd.unknown.10362.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 36 songs; 218 min; rated 2.75/5 by 4 [2]. Said about its sound: The specific copy contains a pause in the tape towards the beginning of the song [15]
- **gd1976-07-12.150658.sbd.c1stGen.miller.flac16**: soundboard; 30 songs; 230 min; rated 2.5/5 by 2 [3]
- **gd1976-07-12.150572.sbd.miller.flac2448**: soundboard; 30 songs; 230 min [4]
- **gd76-07-12.menke.minches.18508.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 23 songs; 162 min; rated 4.25/5 by 4 [6]. Said about its sound: Reviewer praises the quality of the audience recording, dismissing claims that the sound is poor; Franklin's Tower and Dancin' in the Streets are described as sounding like silk; The recording sounds great but seems a bit fast to the listener [12][13][17]

## Around the show

- China Cat teases during Franklin's Tower, making the performance extra special [18]
- The Orpheum Theatre was the smallest venue experienced, with approximately 1,000 seats [19]
- Attendee was particularly swept up during Dancin' in the Streets, possibly hearing it for the first time [19]
- Performance is described as solid but standard fare for the band's 1976 shows [10]
- Music is subdued without high-energy rockers, though the band remained engaged for each song [11]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd76-07-12.sbd.aj.7771.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard - Soundcheck [1]. Also: Soundcheck and Set One lineage involves SBD, VHS, DAT, and CD transfers [1]
- **gd1976-07-12.sbd.unknown.10362.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundcheck: SBD>VHS Master>DAT>CDR; Set1: SBD>MR>R>R>R>DAT>CDR; Set2 SBD>MR>DAT>Sonic Solutions>CDR: [2]
- **gd1976-07-12.150658.sbd.c1stGen.miller.flac16**: taped by Dennis Koda; transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  September 13, 2020; source: SBD > Cassette Master > Cassette (Maxell XLII/Dolby B) [3]. Also: File set is 16-bit at 44.1kHz, sourced from cassettes and patch source [3]
- **gd1976-07-12.150572.sbd.miller.flac2448**: taped by Dennis Koda; transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  September 13, 2020; source: SBD > Cassette Master > Cassette (Maxell XLII/Dolby B) [4]. Also: Sony ECM-270 recorded to cassette master, then transferred to DAT for U.S. Blues [4]
- **gd76-07-12.menke.minches.18508.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Bob Menke; transferred by David Minches; source: Audience Recording: Sony ECM-270s> Sony TC-152 from front of balcony [6]
